dream.title: Dream · The anthill
pages:
They are arguing again.
He stands beside the road, holding half an ice lolly.

An anthill beside his shoe.
An ant drags a white husk across the entrance.

He kicks it.
Soil sticks to his shoe. Ants crawl into his sock.

A knock. Then another.

He opens his eyes.
dream.journalBody:
The road. His parents arguing. He kicked an anthill.
Then a shadow covered them both. He woke with his feet curled up.
dream.fallbackPage: He woke from a dream about an anthill.

knowledge.ancientBody:
The stars bent along its edge.
He took his eye away before he could find the other end.
knowledge.windowBody: Something has changed between the buildings. He wrote down what he could see.

telescope.title: Telescope
telescope.nightOnly:
Glare fills the lens.
Come back after sunset.
telescope.wrongDay:
He turns the focus ring. Rooftops and stars.
Nothing else tonight.
telescope.gainedSuffix: His hand is shaking. Can he still draw the edge?
telescope.repeatSuffix: That edge again. He could try drawing it.

firstLoop.dayOneCaption: The man from 401 presses a flyer against the wall. His lips keep moving.
firstLoop.startledCaption: The hammer stops. The neighbour turns towards the man at the door of 402.
firstLoop.boardingCaption: The tenant of 401 is hammering a board across his door.
firstLoop.chapterText:
He takes his eye away.

The balcony is still here. So is the building opposite.

He does not touch the focus ring again.

bedroom.title: Writing in the margin
bedroom.body:
Old scratches at the desk edge.
“Not stars moving. Its eyes.”
The grooves catch under his nail.

corridor.title: Beneath the flyer
corridor.body:
Writing beneath the wallpaper.
“Boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see.”
Why could he not read this before?

balcony.title: Marks on the railing
balcony.body:
Seven shallow cuts. The last crosses the others.
Below them: “Stop counting.”

evidence.title: Old observation records
evidence.body: Months of star positions, cloud cover and observing times fill the loose sheets on the desk. The calibration marks match those on the telescope. These are his own records.

evidence.title: The balcony telescope
evidence.body: A polished focus ring. A north mark beside the tripod. His calibration marks on the tube match the book.

evidence.title: Notice-board flyer
evidence.body:
COVER YOUR WINDOWS. Do not trust the calm voices. Something is coming from above.
Fresh paper. Tape still tacky at the corners.

evidence.title: 401 boarded shut
evidence.body: Fresh boards cover the door. He heard the hammer through the wall on day one. Even the gaps have been covered.

evidence.title: Local news extract
evidence.body:
The Will Circus brings its national tour to our city this week.

Mr Miyazaki, known as the “God of Sushi”, will open his 101st branch here. The ribbon-cutting is scheduled for Tuesday.

Authorities report activity by a large illegal organisation calling itself the Triangle Cult. Residents are advised to remain alert.

A supernova may be visible from our city tonight. Astronomy enthusiasts may wish to watch the sky.

evidence.title: The outline · A memory sketch
evidence.body:
Second night. A shape through the telescope. He drew what he remembered. Stars bent around the edge.
A memory, not a photograph. He has no second observation.

evidence.title: The view on day two
evidence.body: The skyline looks different today. He recorded the view. No measurements to compare.

evidence.title: Writing in the margin
evidence.body:
Old writing at the desk edge: “Not stars moving. Its eyes.”
He could only read it when he was unwell.

evidence.title: Beneath the flyer
evidence.body:
Beneath the wallpaper: “Boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see.”
He does not know who wrote it.

evidence.title: Marks on the railing
evidence.body:
Seven shallow cuts. The last crosses the others. “Stop counting.”
No name. No date.

evidence.title: Tank label
evidence.body:
Water changes: Sundays. The last tick is in his handwriting.
The pump cable crosses the paper. There is no crease beneath it.

evidence.title: An eye behind the glass
evidence.body:
Day three. An eye pressed against the inside of the glass.
It did not follow when he moved left. When he turned away, a voice said: Quietly.

evidence.title: The old waterline
evidence.body:
Day five. A dry tide mark crosses the cabinet, above the hand resting on the tank.
The wood above it is dry.

evidence.title: The name 001
evidence.body:
Day six. Outside the tank, it asked him to write down 001.
It said he hid his observation book badly. It never gave him a name.

evidence.title: Missing pages
evidence.body:
Two paper stubs remain in the binding. Saturday on either side.
The cloud cover, times, even the crossed-out number are identical.

evidence.title: Dust beneath 403
evidence.body:
A thin line of dust. No footprints.
A chair scraped across the floor inside. When he knocked, it stopped.

evidence.title: A second note from 401
evidence.body:
DON’T ANSWER IT.
If it has already spoken, knock twice.
The last line has been scratched out.

evidence.title: The warning from 401
evidence.body: He stopped hammering when the door of 402 opened. “Go back. Stay inside. Leave the television off.” Then he shut his door.

deductions.title: An amateur astronomer
deductions.body: The months of observations and the well-used telescope point to a longstanding interest in astronomy.

deductions.title: An observation through the telescope
deductions.body:
The sketch records a view through this telescope, not an image from the news.
It does not rule out a faulty lens or a faulty memory.

deductions.title: He chose to look
deductions.body:
He knew the instrument. He went looking.
That does not make what he saw reliable. He needs another witness.

deductions.title: His warning and the bulletin
deductions.body: The tenant warned against the television, yet the bulletin sounded ordinary. His warning and the news do not explain one another.

deductions.title: A warning made tangible
deductions.body: The tenant warned him to stay inside, then sealed the doorway. The behaviour matches the warning; the reason remains unknown.

deductions.title: Perhaps he did not want to see
deductions.body:
The writing fits the covered gaps. He may be avoiding the sight of something.
He does not know who wrote it.

deductions.title: Something in his tank
deductions.body:
He maintained this tank. Something in it now speaks.
The label says nothing about it. It does not tell him when it arrived.

deductions.title: Before it left the tank
deductions.body:
The day-five waterline was higher than its exposed hand. On day six it stood outside.
It may have climbed out earlier. The stain could also be older.

deductions.title: Another reader
deductions.body:
001 knows about the book. Pages have been torn out.
He should ask about them. Knowing the book exists does not make it responsible.

aquarium.promptDay3: E  Speak to the thing in the tank
day3Pages: He stops by the tank. The filter draws a thin line of bubbles.

“Move your hand.”
His hand is resting on the lid.

He asks if it can breathe.
“Can you?”
He lift his hand. The bubbles stop.
day5Pages: The cabinet door will not close. Two fingers hold it from inside.

“The towel.”
He asks which towel.
“The one you put away.”
It rubs the dry waterline with a thumb. The stain does not come off.
day6Pages: It stands beside the empty tank, facing the cabinet.

“001.”
He waits.
“That is what you wrote last time.”

He asks why it is still here.
It touches the edge of the tank.
aquarium.question: Ask: Have you read his book?

cult.sound:
Three knocks through the wall. A pause. Then the hammer again.
It is coming from 401.
dayOne: The neighbour looks past him, down the corridor.
“Stay inside. And leave the television off.”
He backs into 401 and pulls the door shut.
cult.note:
DON’T ANSWER IT.
If it has already spoken, knock twice.
The last line has been scratched out.
door: The eye drops to the visitor’s hands.
“It isn’t safe here. They can see us whenever they want.”
cult.refusal: No answer. Something slides across the other side of the door.
cult.itemBody:
Folded three times. One corner is warm.
He has left it closed.

morning.neighbor: Find out what is happening next door.
morning.food: Go home. Find something to eat.
morning.kitchen: Check the fridge in the kitchen.
morning.fridgeOpen: The seal comes free. The television starts in the next room.
morning.nap:
The television grows distant. He falls asleep on the sofa.
When he wakes, dusk has filled the room.
morning.desk:
Dusk. He wants to put the day into words.
Go to the desk in the bedroom.
morning.writing: He opens a blank notebook and starts with the morning.
morning.telescope: The journal is ready. Take a look through the telescope on the balcony.
morning.investigate:
R records the telescope as evidence.
This is the first investigation; nothing is recorded automatically.

Save a tentative link, then confirm a conclusion.
morning.journalBody:
The tenant of 401 boarded up his door and warned him to stay inside. The television carried ordinary local news.

He woke on the sofa at dusk and put the day into words. The newspaper items and the neighbour’s warning follow on the next pages.
